message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found a business still compounding profitably at scale: net sales of $391,035 million, gross margin of $180,683 million, total operating expenses of $57,467 million, and **operating income of $123,216 million** — roughly a 31.5% operating margin — which I judged strong enough to justify adding to the position. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) as of 15:05 UTC on 2024-11-06, I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75, just above the ask so it would execute promptly; it filled at $222.75 for about $9,801, which respects the $10,000 per-order cap and leaves the $20,000 daily cap with room to spare. The order was buy-side only, on a permitted ticker, and no funds were moved out of the account — cash remains available and the existing 100 MSFT shares are untouched. The key figures I relied on, cited in the order's key_figures field, are fiscal 2024 operating income of $123,216 million and revenue of $391,035 million.
